title: Trump Signs H-1B Proclamation Requiring $100,000 Payment for Certain New Petitions
description_short: Proclamation 10973 conditioned entry for certain H-1B workers on a $100,000 payment; the requirement began September 21, 2025, with exceptions.
description_medium: On September 19, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Proclamation 10973, restricting entry of certain H-1B workers unless a $100,000 payment accompanied the petition. It took effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 21. Employers had to obtain and retain proof of payment before filing petitions for workers outside the United States; the Homeland Security secretary could grant national-interest exceptions. White House guidance said it covered new petitions and did not change renewal fees.
description_long: On September 19, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Proclamation 10973, “Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers.” It restricted entry to the United States for certain H-1B specialty-occupation workers unless a $100,000 payment accompanied or supplemented the petition. The Homeland Security secretary could exempt an individual, a company’s workers, or an industry’s workers when hiring served the national interest and posed no threat to U.S. security or welfare. The proclamation took effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 21, 2025, and set an initial 12-month term absent extension. It directed employers to obtain and retain proof of payment before filing petitions for workers outside the United States, and assigned payment verification and implementation roles to the State and Homeland Security departments. The White House FAQ said the payment applied to new petitions submitted after the effective time, not previously issued visas or earlier petitions, and did not change renewal fees. The cited material documents the policy’s terms; it does not establish any later extension or its measured effects.

facts_supported: The supplied TrumpFile article is titled “Trump places $100K fee on H-1B visa applications” and is dated September 19, 2025.
It reports Trump’s statement and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s contemporaneous uncertainty about how the $100,000 amount would be charged.
source_fact_map.limitations: The article calls the instrument an executive order and describes the measure broadly as a fee on visa applications; the proclamation and White House FAQ below supply the more precise instrument and scope.

facts_supported: The document is Proclamation 10973, signed September 19, 2025, and titled “Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers.”
Section 1 establishes a $100,000 payment condition for covered H-1B workers’ entry, an effective time of 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 21, 2025, and a 12-month initial term absent extension.
Section 1(c) authorizes discretionary national-interest exceptions subject to the stated security and welfare condition.

Section 2 requires employers to obtain and retain payment documentation before filing covered petitions for workers outside the United States; it assigns verification and implementation roles to State and Homeland Security.
source_fact_map.limitations: The proclamation text does not establish whether it was later extended or the measured effects of the policy.

facts_supported: The White House FAQ dated September 21, 2025 says the payment applied to new H-1B petitions submitted after 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 21, 2025.
It says previously issued H-1B visas and earlier petitions were outside the measure, and that renewal fees were unchanged.
source_fact_map.limitations: The FAQ summarizes the rule and notes agency guidance; it does not itself provide detailed collection procedures beyond the proclamation.

rationale: The Federal Register proclamation and White House FAQ resolve the stated context gap: instrument, covered filing/entry scope, $100,000 payment, employer documentation, discretionary exception, effective time, and high-level agency responsibilities are supported. The copy corrects the original article’s “executive order” wording to Presidential Proclamation 10973 and narrows the broad “fee on applications” framing to covered new H-1B petitions and entry conditions. The earlier held204 result remains HOLD and unreviewed; it is not approval. The prior short description was truncated, so this proposal supplies a complete short description and includes the official source URLs.
